catalogs.label: hinton-problems
catalogs.blurb: Geoffrey Hinton's catalog, 1985 to 2022, as runnable stubs.

items.title: encoder-4-2-4
items.paper: Ackley, Hinton & Sejnowski (1985) — A learning algorithm for Boltzmann machines
items.caption: Two groups of 4 visible binary units (V1, V2) connected through 2 hidden binary units. The bottleneck has exactly log2(4) bits of capacity, so the only correct solution puts the 4 training patterns on the 4 corners of {0, 1}^2.

items.title: encoder-3-parity
items.paper: Ackley, Hinton & Sejnowski (1985) — A learning algorithm for Boltzmann machines
items.caption: 3-bit even-parity. The point of this stub is the visible-only Boltzmann hits a hard floor of KL = log 2 ≈ 0.693 (it can only memorize even-cardinality marginals);

items.title: encoder-4-3-4
items.paper: Ackley, Hinton & Sejnowski (1985) — A learning algorithm for Boltzmann machines
items.caption: Over-complete encoder — 3 hidden bits to encode 4 patterns, leaving room for an error-correcting code to emerge. At the right seed the network finds the even-parity codeset (Hamming distance ≥ 2 between any two codes);

items.title: encoder-8-3-8
items.paper: Ackley, Hinton & Sejnowski (1985) — A learning algorithm for Boltzmann machines
items.caption: The information-theoretic minimum: 8 patterns through 3 hidden bits (log2(8) = 3). Hits the paper's reported 16/20 success rate exactly. GIF tracks the 8 hidden codes spreading to the 8 corners of {0, 1}^3.

items.title: encoder-40-10-40
items.paper: Ackley, Hinton & Sejnowski (1985) — A learning algorithm for Boltzmann machines
items.caption: Scale stress-test of the same recipe. With 40 patterns through 10 hidden bits the local-minima problem softens (lots of valid codes) and CD-k recovers cleanly — modern sampling actually beats the 1985 simulated- annealing number.

items.title: xor
items.paper: Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams (1986) — Learning internal representations by error propagation
items.caption: The canonical 2-bit XOR. The decision-surface panel shows the network slicing the unit square along the anti-diagonal once the hidden layer has shaped two well-placed half-planes.

items.title: n-bit-parity
items.paper: Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams (1986) — Learning internal representations by error propagation
items.caption: Generalization of XOR to N bits. Thermometer-coded hidden units can be seen forming as N grows; the difficulty scales as advertised.

items.title: encoder-backprop-8-3-8
items.paper: Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams (1986) — Learning internal representations by error propagation
items.caption: The backprop counterpart to the Boltzmann encoder above. Same problem, different gradient — and 70% of seeds reach exactly 8 distinct hidden codes. Useful side-by-side with encoder-8-3-8 to see what the sampling/temperature schedule buys you.

items.title: distributed-to-local-bottleneck
items.paper: Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams (1986) — Learning internal representations by error propagation
items.caption: Smallest example of a graded single-unit code. One hidden unit must output 4 distinct real values to encode 4 patterns. The animation watches those values pull apart along the unit interval — paper reported (0, 0.2, 0.6, 1.0);

items.title: symmetry
items.paper: Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams (1986) — Learning internal representations by error propagation
items.caption: 6-bit palindrome detection from a single hidden unit. The famous 1 : 2 : 4 antisymmetric weight pattern falls out automatically; the weight Hinton diagram makes the geometric-progression pattern visible by eye at convergence.

items.title: binary-addition
items.paper: Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams (1986) — Learning internal representations by error propagation
items.caption: Two 2-bit numbers in, 3-bit sum out. The interesting story is the local-minima study: a 4-3-3 network solves it;

items.title: negation
items.paper: Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams (1986) — Learning internal representations by error propagation
items.caption: Flag-conditioned bit-flip — one input flag controls whether the other inputs are passed through or flipped.

items.title: t-c-discrimination
items.paper: Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams (1986) — Learning internal representations by error propagation
items.caption: Shared-weight retina discriminating T from C across translations. With weight-tying across spatial positions (the 1986 ancestor of convolutions) the network grows three families of detectors — corner, edge, and T-junction — visible in the kernel…

items.title: recurrent-shift-register
items.paper: Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams (1986) — Learning internal representations by error propagation
items.caption: An RNN learning to be a pure shift register. Both N=3 and N=5 well under the paper's <200-sweep threshold. GIF shows the recurrent state walking through its cycle in lock-step with the input.

items.title: sequence-lookup-25
items.paper: Rumelhart, Hinton & Williams (1986) — Learning internal representations by error propagation
items.caption: A small RNN learning to retrieve which of 25 stored sequences matches a prefix. The viz folder is the largest in the repo (12 PNGs) — per-task attention traces and per-position retrieval curves are worth a look.

items.title: family-trees
items.paper: Hinton (1986) — Learning distributed representations of concepts
items.caption: The original distributed-representations result: an MLP learning two isomorphic kinship trees (English and Italian families) discovers a 6-dimensional code that disentangles generation, branch, and nationality.

items.title: shifter
items.paper: Hinton & Sejnowski (1986) — Learning and relearning in Boltzmann machines
items.caption: The canonical higher-order-feature toy: a Boltzmann machine learning to decide whether two binary input strips are shifted left, right, or not at all.

items.title: grapheme-sememe
items.paper: Hinton & Sejnowski (1986) — Learning and relearning in Boltzmann machines
items.caption: A 4-stage protocol — train, lesion, partial relearning, test — measuring spontaneous recovery: the network re-acquires lesioned associations faster than fresh ones, even without explicit retraining on them.

items.title: riser-spectrogram
items.paper: Plaut & Hinton (1987) — Learning sets of filters using back-propagation
items.caption: Synthetic riser/non-riser spectrogram discrimination. The interesting number is the gap to the analytically-known Bayes optimum: paper reports +1.0pp, we get +0.83pp — a small, real gap that goes away with longer training.

items.title: fast-weights-rehearsal
items.paper: Hinton & Plaut (1987) — Using fast weights to deblur old memories
items.caption: Two-time-scale weights — slow weights store the long-term memory; fast weights pull old memories back into focus when rehearsal stimuli appear. The GIF runs the 4-phase protocol;

eras.name: 1990s — Unsupervised learning, mixtures, the Helmholtz machine

items.title: vowel-mixture-experts
items.paper: Jacobs, Jordan, Nowlan & Hinton (1991) — Adaptive mixtures of local experts
items.caption: Peterson-Barney 4-class vowels in F1/F2 space. The gate's softmax over experts ends up cleanly partitioning the vowel space along phonetic boundaries — exactly the "competing experts" picture the paper sells. 2.7pp gain over a parameter-matched MLP.

items.title: random-dot-stereograms
items.paper: Becker & Hinton (1992) — A self-organizing neural network that discovers surfaces in random-dot stereograms
items.caption: Imax / spatial-coherence objective on synthetic random-dot stereograms. The model discovers depth (disparity) without any depth supervision — pure mutual-information between adjacent receptive fields. Disparity readout R² = 0.74 with no labels.

items.title: sunspots
items.paper: Nowlan & Hinton (1992) — Simplifying neural networks by soft weight-sharing
items.caption: Soft weight-sharing on Wolfer sunspot-count regression. The post-training weight histogram develops two clean Gaussian peaks (one at 0 — pruned weights — and one at 0.27 — shared non-zero value), exactly as the paper predicts.

items.title: spline-images-factorial-vq
items.paper: Hinton & Zemel (1994) — Autoencoders, MDL and Helmholtz free energy
items.caption: Synthetic 5-parameter spline curves rendered to 2D images. The MDL factorial VQ assigns one VQ per latent dimension and beats a single 24-codebook standard-VQ baseline 3×.

items.title: dipole-position
items.paper: Zemel & Hinton (1995) — Learning population codes by minimizing description length
items.caption: 8×8 dipole at random (x, y). Population code emerges as a 2D arrangement of receptive fields tiling the input plane. Needs a brief supervised warm-up to break the symmetry — once broken, R² = 0.81.

items.title: dipole-3d-constraint
items.paper: Zemel & Hinton (1995) — Learning population codes by minimizing description length
items.caption: The 2D positions are constrained to lie on a 3D constraint surface; the network discovers all three dimensions of the manifold.

items.title: dipole-what-where
items.paper: Zemel & Hinton (1995) — Learning population codes by minimizing description length
items.caption: Discontinuous what/where bars — the latent space splits into two perpendicular manifolds (identity vs location). Linear separability 0.58 shows the split, not perfectly clean.

items.title: helmholtz-shifter
items.paper: Dayan, Hinton, Neal & Zemel (1995) — The Helmholtz machine
items.caption: Two-stage generative shifter — recognition net + generative net trained by wake-sleep. 3 of 4 top-layer units become shift-selective; the generative model produces visually plausible shifted samples in the sleep phase shown in the GIF.

items.title: bars
items.paper: Hinton, Dayan, Frey & Neal (1995) — The wake-sleep algorithm
items.caption: The 4×4 horizontal/vertical bars problem — one of the most-cited toy generative-modelling benchmarks. 16-8-1 sigmoid belief net trained by wake-sleep. The KL gap to the paper number (0.451 vs 0.10) is documented as a partial reproduction;

eras.name: 2000s — Products of experts and temporal RBMs

items.title: bars-rbm
items.paper: Hinton (2000) — Training products of experts by minimizing contrastive divergence
items.caption: The same bars problem trained as a CD-k RBM rather than wake-sleep. With 8 hidden units 7 of 8 bars are recovered cleanly; bumping to 16 hidden units recovers all 8. Direct demonstration of why CD made unsupervised learning at scale tractable.

items.title: transforming-pairs
items.paper: Memisevic & Hinton (2007) — Unsupervised learning of image transformations
items.caption: Gated 3-way RBM — the gates encode the transformation between two images, not either image alone.

items.title: bouncing-balls-2
items.paper: Sutskever & Hinton (2007) — Multilevel distributed representations for high-dimensional sequences
items.caption: TRBM video of bouncing balls. Rollout MSE sits between the trivial "copy last frame" and the oracle baselines — model has clearly learned some dynamics but not perfect physics.

items.title: bouncing-balls-3
items.paper: Sutskever, Hinton & Taylor (2008) — The recurrent temporal RBM
items.caption: Same domain at higher resolution (30×30) and the recurrent variant. Reconstruction is tight (0.005 MSE on next-frame given history); free rollout drifts to 0.13 — the classic accumulating-error story.

items.title: transforming-autoencoders
items.paper: Hinton, Krizhevsky & Wang (2011) — Transforming auto-encoders
items.caption: The seed of the capsules program. Each capsule outputs a small pose vector (dx, dy) per part; reconstruction is gated through that pose.

items.title: deep-lambertian-spheres
items.paper: Tang, Salakhutdinov & Hinton (2012) — Deep Lambertian Networks
items.caption: Synthetic spheres rendered under multiple lighting directions. The model recovers surface normals (27° angular error) and albedo (7× better than naive baseline) by separating shading from reflectance — the intrinsic-images problem cast as inverse…

items.title: rnn-pathological
items.paper: Sutskever, Martens, Dahl & Hinton (2013) — On the importance of initialization and momentum
items.caption: The Hochreiter-Schmidhuber long-term-dependency battery. 3 of 4 tasks solved; orthogonal initialization beats random Gaussian init by a clear margin in the wallclock-to-converge curve.

items.title: distillation-mnist-omitted-3
items.paper: Hinton, Vinyals & Dean (2015) — Distilling the knowledge in a neural network
items.caption: The classic "student never sees a 3" demonstration. Soft-target distillation transfers enough information about digit 3 from the teacher's logits that, after a per-class bias correction, the student classifies 3s at 97.82%.

items.title: air-multimnist
items.paper: Eslami et al. (2016) — Attend, Infer, Repeat
items.caption: Variable-count MNIST scenes — the model decides how many objects are in the image, then attends to and reconstructs each. Object-count accuracy 79.7%; reconstructions blurry. The GIF visualizes the per-step attention windows opening one at a time.

items.title: air-3d-primitives
items.paper: Eslami et al. (2016) — Attend, Infer, Repeat
items.caption: Same AIR machinery, but the renderer is a small 3D primitive engine and the inference network must invert it. Cleanly recovers 1-primitive scenes; 3-primitive count accuracy 81%.

items.title: fast-weights-associative-retrieval
items.paper: Ba, Hinton, Mnih, Leibo & Ionescu (2016) — Using fast weights to attend to the recent past
items.caption: faithful; retrieval rate 38% short of paper. The fast-weight matrix (visualized as a heatmap that grows then decays) is the visualization star here.

items.title: multi-level-glimpse-mnist
items.paper: Ba, Hinton, Mnih, Leibo & Ionescu (2016) — Using fast weights to attend to the recent past
items.caption: 24 hierarchical glimpses on MNIST. The GIF traces the glimpse trajectory across the digit — a clean visualization of attention-as-control even at the modest 82% accuracy.

items.title: catch-game
items.paper: Ba, Hinton, Mnih, Leibo & Ionescu (2016) — Using fast weights to attend to the recent past
items.caption: A partial-observability paddle/ball game where the network must integrate information across time to catch the ball. Fast-weights variant beats the vanilla RNN 33.9% to 11.4% at size=20 (paper-scale); reaches 91% at the easier size=10 setting.

items.title: multimnist-capsnet
items.paper: Sabour, Frosst & Hinton (2017) — Dynamic routing between capsules
items.caption: Overlapping digit pairs. The network must decompose a single image into two simultaneous classifications — exactly the case capsules were designed for. 22× above chance at 48.6% on this hard split, but well short of paper.

items.title: affnist
items.paper: Sabour, Frosst & Hinton (2017) — Dynamic routing between capsules
items.caption: Train on translated MNIST, test on affNIST (additional rotations and shears). The paper claimed CapsNet generalizes to novel viewpoints better than a parameter-matched CNN by +13%; we get the opposite sign.

items.title: smallnorb-novel-viewpoint
items.paper: Hinton, Sabour & Frosst (2018) — Matrix capsules with EM routing
items.caption: Synthesized NORB-style objects, held-out azimuth/elevation at test time. Matrix capsules edge out a parameter-matched CNN on the held-out viewpoint split — the qualitative claim of the paper holds, with smaller absolute numbers.

items.title: constellations
items.paper: Kosiorek, Sabour, Teh & Hinton (2019) — Stacked capsule autoencoders
items.caption: 2D point-cloud part-whole grouping. The model groups individual points into the constellations they came from with no supervision — 86.9% per- point recovery at the best seed.

items.title: mnist-2x5-subclass
items.paper: Müller, Kornblith & Hinton (2020) — Subclass distillation
items.caption: A super-class teacher trained on {0..4} vs {5..9} two-class labels; the student receives the teacher's logits, which carry hidden subclass information.

items.title: geo-flow-capsules
items.paper: Sabour, Tagliasacchi, Yazdani, Hinton & Fleet (2021) — Unsupervised part representation by flow capsules
items.caption: Geo / Geo+ moving 2D shapes — the model decomposes each frame into parts using only motion (optical-flow consistency) as supervision. Mean IoU 0.764 against ground-truth part masks vs chance 0.20.

items.title: ellipse-world
items.paper: Culp, Sabour & Hinton (2022) — Testing GLOM's ability to infer wholes from ambiguous parts
items.caption: eGLOM-lite for the ambiguous-part-to-whole test. Each frame of the GIF is one iteration of the GLOM column dynamics; you can watch islands of agreement form across iterations as ambiguous local parts commit to a consistent global whole.

items.title: ff-hybrid-mnist
items.paper: Hinton (2022) — The forward-forward algorithm
items.caption: FF unsupervised MLP with hand-crafted hybrid-image negatives. The GIF shows the negative-sample construction (images literally averaged in pixel space). Test error 5.21% — works, but does not match paper's 1.37%.

items.title: ff-label-in-input
items.paper: Hinton (2022) — The forward-forward algorithm
items.caption: The label one-hot is concatenated to the first 10 pixels of the image, then FF is run with the correct label as positive and a wrong label as negative. Closer to paper than the hybrid variant (3.60% vs 1.36%).

items.title: ff-recurrent-mnist
items.paper: Hinton (2022) — The forward-forward algorithm
items.caption: The "video" variant — the same MNIST frame repeated for several timesteps with top-down recurrent connections so each layer can use the next layer's previous-step activity as context.

items.title: ff-cifar-locally-connected
items.paper: Hinton (2022) — The forward-forward algorithm
items.caption: CIFAR-10 with a locally-connected (not weight-tied) FF network. FF beats a parameter-matched BP baseline on this architecture (22.78% vs 38.31% test err) — one of the few places in the suite where FF wins outright.

items.title: ff-aesop-sequences
items.paper: Hinton (2022) — The forward-forward algorithm
items.caption: Next-character prediction on Aesop's Fables with self-generated negatives — the negatives come from the model's own previous-step predictions. Teacher-forced 53%, self-generated 34%, well above any of the non-FF baselines (3–20%).

catalogs.label: schmidhuber-problems
catalogs.blurb: Jürgen Schmidhuber's catalog, 1989 onward, as runnable stubs.

eras.name: 1980s — Local rules and the Neural Bucket Brigade

items.title: nbb-xor
items.paper: Schmidhuber (1989) — A local learning algorithm for dynamic feedforward and recurrent networks
items.caption: XOR via the Neural Bucket Brigade — a strictly local-in-space-and-time, winner-take-all, dissipative learning rule. There is no backprop, no RTRL, no gradient.

items.title: nbb-moving-light
items.paper: Schmidhuber (1989) — A local learning algorithm for dynamic feedforward and recurrent networks
items.caption: 1-D moving-light direction discrimination via the same NBB rule extended to a small fully-recurrent net (5 retina cells + bias → 2 output units forming a WTA subset).

items.title: flip-flop
items.paper: Schmidhuber (1990) — Making the world differentiable
items.caption: The 1990 paper sets up a tiny non-stationary control task that has all the ingredients of the long-time-lag problem Hochreiter would later formalise as the vanishing-gradient barrier.

items.title: pole-balance-non-markov
items.paper: Schmidhuber (1990) — Making the world differentiable
items.caption: Cart-pole balancing where the controller observes only positions, not velocities. The 4-D real state is (x, x_dot, θ, θ_dot), but C only sees (x, θ). M predicts next observed positions from action + history; C trained by BP through M's gradient.

items.title: pole-balance-markov-vac
items.paper: Schmidhuber (1990) — Recurrent networks adjusted by adaptive critics
items.caption: Standard cart-pole, Markov regime: the controller observes the full state at every step. K=2 vector-valued critic with two qualitatively distinct components (V_pole saturates near 1/(1-γ)=100; V_cart tracks live 1−|x|/2.4 margin).

items.title: saccadic-target-detection
items.paper: Schmidhuber & Huber (1990) — Learning to generate focus trajectories
items.caption: Active visual attention. The controller must move a small fovea over a 2-D scene to find a target halo, given only the local pixels under the fovea. C is feedforward; M predicts the change in halo at the next fovea position.

items.title: curiosity-three-regions
items.paper: Schmidhuber (1991) — Adaptive confidence and adaptive curiosity
items.caption: A 1-D environment partitioned into three regions: deterministic / random / learnable-but-unlearned. Curiosity reward = windowed reduction in M's prediction error.

items.title: subgoal-obstacle-avoidance
items.paper: Schmidhuber (1991) — Learning to generate sub-goals for action sequences
items.caption: Hierarchical RL: a sub-goal generator C_high proposes K=2 waypoints, a low-level controller C_low (intentionally obstacle-blind, input = rel_target only) steers toward each.

items.title: pomdp-flag-maze
items.paper: Schmidhuber (1991) — Reinforcement learning in Markovian and non-Markovian environments
items.caption: A 2-D T-maze with a hidden flag. The agent observes only its local 4-wall context plus a 1-bit indicator that is non-zero ONLY at the start cell. Recurrent M+C architecture must latch the indicator across the full episode.

items.title: chunker-22-symbol
items.paper: Schmidhuber (1991/1992) — Neural sequence chunkers
items.caption: 22-symbol alphabet streamed without episode boundaries. Two-network history compression: automatizer A predicts next symbol; chunker C only receives A's prediction failures (surprises). The 20-step lag bridge that vanilla BPTT/RTRL fails on.

items.title: fast-weights-unknown-delay
items.paper: Schmidhuber (1992) — Learning to control fast-weight memories
items.caption: Two arbitrary input signals must be associated across a time gap of unknown length. Slow programmer net S (917 params, 4 heads: key/value/query/gate); W_fast updated as W_fast += eta · g_t · outer(v_t, k_t).

items.title: fast-weights-key-value
items.paper: Schmidhuber (1992) — Learning to control fast-weight memories
items.caption: A sequence of (key, value) pairs is presented one step at a time. Each step writes an outer-product update into a fast weight matrix. Retrieval = W_fast · k_query.

items.title: predictability-min-binary-factors
items.paper: Schmidhuber (1992) — Learning factorial codes by predictability minimization
items.caption: Given an observable x produced by a fixed random linear mixing of K independent binary factors, learn an encoder E: x → y that produces a factorial code. Adversarial setup: encoder maximizes per-component predictor MSE; predictors minimize it.

eras.name: 1993 — Predictable classifications, self-reference, very deep chunking

items.title: predictable-stereo
items.paper: Schmidhuber & Prelinger (1993) — Discovering predictable classifications
items.caption: Predictability maximization — the dual of PM. Two networks each see one view of the same synthetic stereo scene; their job is to produce scalar codes that maximally agree.

items.title: self-referential-weight-matrix
items.paper: Schmidhuber (1993) — A self-referential weight matrix
items.caption: A recurrent network whose weight matrix is itself part of the state. W_eff = W_slow + W_fast. Slow params trained by BPTT across episodes; fast plastic matrix is reset each episode and rewritten by the network's own outputs every step.

items.title: chunker-very-deep-1200
items.paper: Schmidhuber (1993) — Habilitationsschrift
items.caption: The Habilitationsschrift's "very deep learning" demonstration: the two-network neural sequence chunker doing credit assignment over roughly 1200 unrolled time-steps. Effective BPTT depth T - 1 = 1199 (raw) compresses to 2 (chunker on surprises).

eras.name: 1995–1997 — Levin search and the LSTM benchmark suite

items.title: levin-count-inputs
items.paper: Schmidhuber (1995/1997) — Discovering solutions with low Kolmogorov complexity
items.caption: Find a program that maps a 100-bit input to its popcount from only 3 training examples — without gradient descent. Levin search enumerates programs ordered by len(p) + log(t). Found program: 5-instr PUSH0 HERE BIT ADD LOOP.

items.title: levin-add-positions
items.paper: Schmidhuber (1995/1997) — Discovering solutions with low Kolmogorov complexity
items.caption: Same Levin enumeration, different target: index-sum of the bit positions where the input is 1 (induces the linear weight vector w_i = i). Found program: length-3 im+. 58 evaluations to find; 200/200 generalize on held-out.

items.title: rs-two-sequence
items.paper: Hochreiter & Schmidhuber (1996) — LSTM can solve hard long time lag problems
items.caption: Bengio-94 latch task. Random-weight-guessing on a small fully-recurrent net solves what BPTT/RTRL fails on. The point is the algorithm: just sample weights uniformly, run forward, score. No mutation, no crossover, no gradient.

items.title: rs-parity
items.paper: Hochreiter & Schmidhuber (1996) — LSTM can solve hard long time lag problems
items.caption: N-bit sequence parity (XOR of all input bits) by random weight guessing on a small recurrent net. The parity solution lives in a narrow weight-space basin RS happens to hit by chance. N=50 seed 0: 10,253 trials / 15.3s;

items.title: rs-tomita
items.paper: Hochreiter & Schmidhuber (1996) — LSTM can solve hard long time lag problems
items.caption: Random-weight guessing on Tomita grammars #1 (a), #2 ((ab)), and #4 (no aaa substring). Three regular languages of increasing difficulty. All 3 grammars solved across 10 seeds; trial counts within ~3× of paper for #1/#2, ~6× for #4.

items.title: adding-problem
items.paper: Hochreiter & Schmidhuber (1997) — Long Short-Term Memory canonical battery
items.caption: T=100 sequences with 2-D inputs: random reals + sparse markers. Target = sum of the 2 marked values. The first non-trivial LSTM benchmark. LSTM MSE 0.0007 (50× under paper's 0.04 threshold); vanilla RNN MSE 0.0706 (gradient vanishes);

items.title: embedded-reber
items.paper: Hochreiter & Schmidhuber (1997) — Long Short-Term Memory canonical battery
items.caption: Reber grammar wrapped with outer T/P matching pair (long-range dependency). Original 1997 LSTM (input + output gate, no forget gate). 10/10 seeds, mean 4800 sequences vs paper 8440 — 1.8× faster with Adam + negative gate-bias init.

items.title: noise-free-long-lag
items.paper: Hochreiter & Schmidhuber (1997) — Long Short-Term Memory canonical battery
items.caption: Two locally-encoded sequences (y, a₁,…,a_{p−1}, y) and (x, a₁,…,a_{p−1}, x). Sub-variant (a) at p=50: solved at sequence 600. Last-step gradient weighting trick (×100) keeps Adam's per-step normalisation from drowning out the rare long-lag signal.

items.title: two-sequence-noise
items.paper: Hochreiter & Schmidhuber (1997) — Long Short-Term Memory canonical battery
items.caption: Variant 3c (target noise σ=0.32). Canonical 1997 LSTM, 3 blocks × 2 cells = 6 cells, 103 params. Output-gate biases per block = -2, -4, -6 (paper's recipe). 4/4 seeds 100% accuracy on noiseless test sequences.

items.title: multiplication-problem
items.paper: Hochreiter & Schmidhuber (1997) — Long Short-Term Memory canonical battery
items.caption: Same as adding-problem but target = product of the 2 marked values. LSTM with forget gate (Gers 2000). MSE 0.0028 at T=30 (17× chance); 3/5 seeds converge — paper-faithful per-seed brittleness.

items.title: temporal-order-3bit
items.paper: Hochreiter & Schmidhuber (1997) — Long Short-Term Memory canonical battery
items.caption: Two information-carrying symbols X, Y at unknown positions; classify the temporal order (XX, XY, YX, YY). Original 1997 LSTM (no forget gate). 5/5 seeds 100%, median ~6.4k seqs vs paper 31,390 (Adam advantage). Vanilla RNN at chance 0.25.

items.title: pipe-symbolic-regression
items.paper: Salustowicz & Schmidhuber (1997) — Probabilistic Incremental Program Evolution
items.caption: Symbolic regression on Koza's classic benchmark f(x) = x⁴ + x³ + x² + x. Probabilistic Prototype Tree (PPT) over {+, −, *, /, x, R}. PBIL update toward elite at every visited node; per-component mutation along elite path. No gradient, no crossover.

items.title: pipe-6-bit-parity
items.paper: Salustowicz & Schmidhuber (1997) — Probabilistic Incremental Program Evolution
items.caption: Same PIPE machinery on Boolean function set {AND, OR, NOT, IF, x_0..x_5}. Bitmask program evaluator runs all 64 inputs in O(tree_size) bitwise ops. 4-bit even parity solves cleanly at gen 258 (16/16); 6-bit reaches 71.9% at the 240s budget cap.

items.title: ssa-bias-transfer-mazes
items.paper: Schmidhuber, Zhao, Wiering (1997) — Shifting inductive bias with SSA
items.caption: Success-story algorithm: keep a stack of policy modifications; only retain modifications that produce statistically significant lifetime-reward improvements (history-conditioned, not per-task). Bias from one task transfers to the next.

items.title: hq-learning-pomdp
items.paper: Wiering & Schmidhuber (1997) — HQ-learning
items.caption: Hierarchical Q(λ) for POMDP. M sub-agents with their own Q-tables; control transfers between sub-agents at sub-goal observations. Honest non-replication: paper's HQ-vs-flat gap doesn't reproduce on the 29-cell maze.

items.title: semilinear-pm-image-patches
items.paper: Schmidhuber, Eldracher, Foltin (1996) — Semilinear PM
items.caption: Linear encoder y = Wx on the Stiefel manifold (polar projection after every step). Predictor input is the standardised squared code z = (y² - μ) / σ (the squaring is the one nonlinearity — "semilinear").

items.title: lococode-ica
items.paper: Hochreiter & Schmidhuber (1999) — LOCOCODE
items.caption: Tied autoencoder + L1 sparsity on whitened input (surrogate for the paper's flat-minimum-search Hessian penalty). On synthetic Laplacian sources: Amari distance 0.093 — 4× better than PCA (0.388), within 5× of FastICA (0.022).

items.title: continual-embedded-reber
items.paper: Gers, Schmidhuber, Cummins (2000) — Learning to forget
items.caption: Embedded Reber strings concatenated without any episode reset. Mechanism contrast made visible: forget-gate LSTM cell-state norm stabilizes at ~25; no-forget-gate norm grows to ~295 across the stream. Forget gates drop at end-of-string offsets.

items.title: anbn-anbncn
items.paper: Gers & Schmidhuber (2001) — Context-free and context-sensitive languages
items.caption: Two formal languages: a^n b^n (context-free) and a^n b^n c^n (context-sensitive). Peephole LSTM (Gers 2002 cell). Cell 0 emerges as a clean linear counter — charges during a's, discharges during b's. Trained n=1..10 → generalizes a^n b^n to n=1..65;

items.title: timing-counting-spikes
items.paper: Gers, Schraudolph, Schmidhuber (2002) — Learning precise timing
items.caption: Measure-Spike-Distance (MSD): two input spikes at t1 < t2; network must fire at t1 + 2·(t2 - t1). Peephole LSTM (cell state feeds gates). One cell develops an analog interval timer across the inter-spike gap.

items.title: blues-improvisation
items.paper: Eck & Schmidhuber (2002) — Blues improvisation
items.caption: 12-bar bebop blues. Fixed chord progression: C7 C7 C7 C7 / F7 F7 C7 C7 / G7 F7 C7 C7. 2-layer stacked LSTM (chord layer H1=20 → melody layer H2=24). 8 hand-synthesized 12-bar choruses (no external MIDI). 12/12 bar-onset chord match;

items.title: evolino-sines-mackey-glass
items.paper: Schmidhuber, Wierstra, Gomez (2005/2007) — Evolino
items.caption: Hybrid neuroevolution + linear regression for sequence learning. LSTM hidden weights evolved by population selection + gaussian mutation + crossover;

items.title: double-pole-no-velocity
items.paper: Gomez & Schmidhuber (2005) — Co-evolving recurrent neurons
items.caption: Cart with two stacked poles of different lengths (canonical hard non-Markov RL benchmark). Hidden velocities — only positions observed. Wieland 1991 double cart-pole sim in numpy, RK4 integration.

items.title: timit-blstm-ctc
items.paper: Graves et al. (2005/2006) — BLSTM and Connectionist Temporal Classification
items.caption: Synthetic phoneme corpus (K=6 phonemes, 8 mel-like bands, co-articulated shared-onset clusters so future context disambiguates). Bidirectional LSTM + log-space CTC forward-backward. BLSTM 1.87× faster than uni-LSTM (5/5 seeds 300 vs 560 iters);

items.title: iam-handwriting
items.paper: Graves, Liwicki, Fernández, Bertolami, Bunke, Schmidhuber (2009) — Unconstrained handwriting
items.caption: 10-character hand-crafted alphabet, each glyph from ellipse arcs + line segments; 47-word vocab; per-word affine slant + per-point Gaussian jitter. BLSTM + CTC reads pen-trajectory data. In-vocab CER 0.082 / word acc 0.77;

items.title: oops-towers-of-hanoi
items.paper: Schmidhuber (2002–2004) — Optimal Ordered Problem Solver
items.caption: Towers of Hanoi: move n disks from peg 0 to peg 2; optimal solution length 2^n - 1. OOPS = Levin search with reusable subroutines. Discovers 6-token recursive solver SD C SD M SA C at n=3; reuses with zero search from n=4 onward.

items.title: mnist-deep-mlp
items.paper: Cireşan, Meier, Gambardella, Schmidhuber (2010) — Deep, big, simple nets
items.caption: MNIST classification with a plain feedforward MLP — no convolution, no pretraining, no model averaging — on heavily deformed training data. Per-batch affine + Simard elastic deformation in pure numpy (separable Gaussian + bilinear sampling).

items.title: mcdnn-image-bench
items.paper: Cireşan, Meier, Schmidhuber (2012) — Multi-column DNN
items.caption: Single-column 4-layer ReLU MLP on MNIST (paper's multi-column ensemble + GTSRB/CASIA deferred to v1.5). 1.46% test err; multi-seed mean 1.47% ± 0.03%. Honest gap: paper 35-column ensemble 0.23%, single CNN ~0.4%.

items.title: em-segmentation-isbi
items.paper: Cireşan, Giusti, Gambardella, Schmidhuber (2012) — EM segmentation
items.caption: Synthetic Voronoi-EM substitute for ISBI 2012 stack: random Voronoi tessellation + dark 1-px boundaries + per-cell intensity + Gaussian noise + sparse organelles + 3×3 PSF blur. MLP pixel classifier on 32×32 patches.

items.title: compete-to-compute
items.paper: Srivastava, Masci, Kazerounian, Gomez, Schmidhuber (2013) — Compete to compute
items.caption: LWTA (Local Winner-Take-All): groups of k=2 units per layer; only the per-group winner forwards activations, others zero out; gradient flows only through the winner. Sequential 2-task MNIST split (digits 0-4 → 5-9).

items.title: highway-networks
items.paper: Srivastava, Greff, Schmidhuber (2015) — Highway Networks
items.caption: Gated deep MLP: y = H(x)·T(x) + x·(1−T(x)) with learned sigmoid gate T. Depth comparison 5/10/20/30/50: highway stable at all depths (0.926 at depth 30); plain MLP dies past depth 10 (stuck at chance 0.124).

items.title: lstm-search-space-odyssey
items.paper: Greff, Srivastava, Koutník, Steunebrink, Schmidhuber (2017) — LSTM Search Space Odyssey
items.caption: 8 LSTM variants in one ablation matrix: V (vanilla), NIG (no input gate), NFG (no forget gate), NOG (no output gate), NIAF (no input activation), NOAF (no output activation), CIFG (coupled input-forget), NP (no peepholes).

items.title: clockwork-rnn
items.paper: Koutník, Greff, Gomez, Schmidhuber (2014) — Clockwork RNN
items.caption: Standard Elman RNN with hidden layer partitioned into G modules. Each module g has a clock period T_g; at timestep t a module updates only when t mod T_g == 0. Forward connections only flow from slower clocks to faster clocks.

items.title: torcs-vision-evolution
items.paper: Koutník, Cuccu, Schmidhuber, Gomez (2013) — Vision-based RL via evolution
items.caption: Numpy oval racing track + 16×16 pixel observation. MLP 256→16→1 with W1 parameterized by a 4×4=16 low-frequency 2-D DCT block per hidden unit (decoded via precomputed orthonormal IDCT-II matrix).

items.title: neural-em-shapes
items.paper: Greff, van Steenkiste, Schmidhuber (2017) — Neural EM
items.caption: Unsupervised perceptual grouping. K=3 slot Neural EM with manual BPTT through T=4 unrolled EM iterations. E-step softmax over pixel likelihoods, M-step tanh recurrence on bottlenecked H=24 (forces specialisation).

items.title: relational-nem-bouncing-balls
items.paper: van Steenkiste, Chang, Greff, Schmidhuber (2018) — Relational Neural EM
items.caption: Bouncing balls with elastic equal-mass collisions. Oracle 4-D slot state (x, y, vx, vy). Non-relational baseline: MLP_dyn(s_k); relational: MLP_msg(s_k, s_j) → mean aggregation → MLP_dyn(s_k, agg_k). Relational wins K=3,4,5;

eras.name: 2018–2025 — World models, fast-weight Transformers, systematic generalization

items.title: world-models-carracing
items.paper: Ha & Schmidhuber (2018) — Recurrent World Models
items.caption: Numpy 2-D top-down racing track substitute for CarRacing-v0. Centerline = closed loop generated from low-frequency sinusoids; agent observes a 16×16 patch of mask, rotated to car frame.

items.title: world-models-vizdoom-dream
items.paper: Ha & Schmidhuber (2018) — Recurrent World Models
items.caption: Numpy 5×5 gridworld dodging-fireballs analog of DoomTakeCover. The paper's "DoomRNN dream" experiment: controller C is trained ENTIRELY inside M's rollouts (no real-env interaction during training), then transferred zero-shot to the real env.

items.title: upside-down-rl
items.paper: Schmidhuber et al. (2019) — Reinforcement Learning Upside Down
items.caption: Standard RL fits a value function or policy gradient. UDRL inverts: the policy is a supervised mapping from (state, desired_return, time_horizon) → action. Numpy 9-state chain MDP per SPEC's RL-stub rule (paper used LunarLanderSparse).

items.title: linear-transformers-fwp
items.paper: Schlag, Irie, Schmidhuber (2021) — Linear Transformers ARE Fast Weight Programmers
items.caption: The cleanest result of the catalog: linear self-attention V^T(Kq) and the 1992 fast-weight programmer (V^T K)q compute the same numpy expression. Equivalence verified to 2.22e-16 (1 ulp at float64) on every input tested.

items.title: neural-data-router
items.paper: Csordás, Irie, Schmidhuber (2022) — The Neural Data Router
items.caption: Compositional table lookup: 4 values × 4 functions × depth-d expressions. NDR adds two switches to a Transformer: geometric attention (per-query distance-ordered scan, "stop at first match") + per-position copy gate.
